Decisions we've put off, so they aren't lost. Each one says where it came up and what it affects. When one is settled, record the answer where it belongs (`CONTEXT.md`, an ADR or a ticket) and tick it off here.

- [ ] **Does a Current Entry need a start date?** `CONTEXT.md` says a Current Entry "has a start date but no end date", but the spec (#1, story 54) makes every date optional. Either reword the glossary, or make Current require a start date, which would change `setCurrent` and the date component (#23).

items.title: Streamline the editor's loading and not-found states

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue

items.body:
## Parent

#1

## Problem

After #10, opening a Resume in the editor goes through two loading phases, each with its own wording and layout:

| Stage | Where | What the user sees |
|---|---|---|
| Server HTML, until the page's scripts run and the Resume is read | `EditorLoader` | Full-screen "Loading…", with no top bar |
| Unknown id / storage blocked | `EditorLoader` | Full-screen "Not found!" (with a link back) or the storage error, with no top bar |
| Resume read; Theme still loading | `Editor` → `PreviewPane` (`useTheme`) | Top bar and panes appear; the preview says "Loading preview…" |
| Theme loaded | `PreviewPane` | The Ledger page |

What's wrong with it:

1. **Two loading messages in a row** ("Loading…", then "Loading preview…"), for what is really one wait: getting the screen ready.
2. **The layout jumps** from a bare full-screen message to the whole editor.
3. **The first message mostly waits for the page's scripts, not for data.** Reading localStorage takes almost no time. The Theme import only starts after that, so it waits for the scripts too.
4. **Export PDF is clickable while the Theme loads, but does nothing.** Export needs the Theme's page to print.
5. **Three near-identical message components:** `EditorMessage`, `PreviewMessage` and the Library's `LibraryMessage`.

## Direction (preferred)

Show the editor's layout at once, and fill it in as things load:

- The **top bar** shows immediately. **Export PDF is disabled** until the Resume and its Theme have both loaded.
- The **Content pane** shows a **skeleton** while the Resume is read.
- The **Preview pane** shows a matching note (like "Loading preview…") until the Resume and Theme are ready. After that, its only note is "Nothing to preview yet".
- Each part renders as soon as what it needs has loaded.

This keeps #10's rule that the Theme never blocks the top bar or the Content pane.

## Alternative considered

**One loading phase.** `EditorLoader` loads the Resume and its Theme before showing the Editor. The Theme still loads from its own file, and its import can start as soon as the page's scripts run, alongside the Resume read. The Editor always gets a Theme, so "Loading preview…", `useTheme` and the export-before-load case all go away. It's simpler, but the top bar and Content pane wait for the Theme too, which goes against #10's rule. Not preferred, because the direction above renders each part as soon as it can.

## Open question: an unknown id (and storage errors)

The editor currently shows plain "Not found!" text with a "Back to resumes" link, and a plain message when storage is blocked. Both are stand-ins. To decide:

- Should these screens keep the editor layout (the top bar, at least), or be separate full-screen pages?
- What should they say, and which ways out should they offer (back to the Library, create a new Resume)?
- Should they share one message component with the Library and the preview?

Settle this before building, or split it into its own ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a Resume never shows two loading messages one after the other, and the layout doesn't jump from a full-screen message to the editor
- [ ] The Content pane shows a skeleton while the Resume loads
- [ ] The Preview pane shows a single loading note until it can draw the Theme's page
- [ ] Export PDF is disabled until the Resume and its Theme have loaded
- [ ] Loading and error text is announced to screen readers
- [ ] The not-found and storage-error screens follow the decision on the open question above

## Blocked by

- #10 Editor page shell: load a Resume, handle not-found, two-pane layout

items.body:
## Problem Statement

Tech job seekers tailor their resume for almost every application: a different Summary for backend vs. full-stack roles, dropping an irrelevant project, cutting two Bullets from an old job, hiding a Skill that doesn't fit. With today's tools that means juggling many near-identical files, re-typing content, and losing track of which version says what. Most resume builders also force a sign-up before you can even try them.

## Solution

Linted v1 is a local-first resume builder that runs entirely in the browser, with no account. A user keeps any number of independent Resumes, each with a Resume Title. The editor shows Content on one side and a live preview on the other, rendered in a Theme. Every Section, Entry, Bullet and Skill can be Enabled or Disabled, so a user can keep several alternative Summaries or extra Bullets in one Resume and switch between them with a click; only Enabled, non-Empty Content appears in the preview and the Export. When a user wants a variant, they Duplicate a Resume and edit the copy freely. Export produces an A4 PDF that matches the preview exactly.

## User Stories

### Resume list

1. As a job seeker, I want to use Linted without signing up, so that I can start building immediately.
2. As a job seeker, I want to see all my Resumes in one list, so that I can find the one I need.
3. As a job seeker, I want the list to show each Resume's Resume Title, so that I can tell Resumes apart.
4. As a job seeker, I want the list ordered by most recently edited, so that my active Resumes are at the top.
5. As a job seeker, I want to see when each Resume was last edited, so that I know which version is freshest.
6. As a job seeker, I want a "create" button on the list, so that I can start a new Resume.
7. As a job seeker, I want creating a Resume to take me straight into its editor, so that I can start writing right away.
8. As a job seeker, I want to open any Resume from the list, so that I can continue editing it.
9. As a job seeker, I want each Resume to have its own stable link, so that I can bookmark it or come back to it.
10. As a job seeker, I want to Duplicate a Resume, so that I can tailor a variant without touching the original.
11. As a job seeker, I want a Duplicate to be titled "<original title> (copy)" by default, so that I can tell it came from the original.
12. As a job seeker, I want edits to a Duplicate never to affect the original (and vice versa), so that each Resume is safe to change.
13. As a job seeker, I want to delete a Resume, so that I can clear out versions I no longer need.
14. As a job seeker, I want to confirm before a Resume is deleted, so that I don't lose work by accident, since there is no way to recover it.
15. As a job seeker, I want a friendly "not found" screen with a way back to my list if I open a link to a Resume that doesn't exist, so that I'm not stuck.
16. As a job seeker, I want an empty-state message on the list when I have no Resumes yet, so that I know what to do first.

### Resume Title

17. As a job seeker, I want to rename a Resume, so that its Resume Title reflects what it's for (e.g. "Stripe backend v2").
18. As a job seeker, I want to be allowed to give two Resumes the same Resume Title, so that the app doesn't get in my way.
19. As a job seeker, I want to be prevented from saving an empty Resume Title, so that every Resume stays identifiable in the list.

### New Resume

20. As a job seeker, I want a new Resume to start with a Header, Summary, Experience, Projects, Skills and Education Section, so that I can see the usual structure immediately.
21. As a job seeker, I want those starting Sections to be Empty (no dummy text), so that I don't have to delete placeholder content.
22. As a job seeker, I want Empty Sections and Entries not to appear in the preview, so that a half-filled Resume still looks clean.

### Editor layout and saving

23. As a job seeker, I want the editor split into Content and preview, so that I see the effect of every change as I make it.
24. As a job seeker, I want every change saved automatically, so that I never lose work by forgetting to save.
25. As a job seeker, I want my Resumes to still be there after I close and reopen the browser, so that I can work over several sessions.

### Header

26. As a job seeker, I want to enter my name and headline (e.g. "Senior Backend Engineer") in the Header, so that the top of my resume introduces me.
27. As a job seeker, I want to add contact items (email, phone, location, and any number of links), so that recruiters can reach me.
28. As a job seeker, I want each link to have a label and a URL, so that it reads well (e.g. "GitHub").
29. As a job seeker, I want to Disable individual contact items, so that, for example, I can hide my phone number on one Resume.
30. As a job seeker, I want the Header always first in its part of the page, so that my name comes first.
31. As a job seeker, I want every Resume to always have exactly one Header, so that my personal details can't be lost by accident.
32. ~~As a job seeker, I want "add Header" to be offered only when my Resume has no Header, so that I can't end up with two.~~ Dropped: the Header can't be deleted, so it never needs adding back.
33. As a job seeker, I want the Header's title to be fixed, so that it behaves consistently.

### Sections

34. As a job seeker, I want to rename any Section other than the Header (e.g. "Experience" → "Professional Experience"), so that headings match my style.
35. As a job seeker, I want to delete a Custom Section, so that I can remove things I'll never use. A Default Section can't be deleted; I leave it Empty or Disable it instead.
36. ~~As a job seeker, I want to add another Section of any Default Section type (e.g. a second Experience Section called "Teaching"), so that I can split my history however I like.~~ Moved to a later version: a Resume has exactly one of each Default Section.
37. As a job seeker, I want to add any number of Custom Sections with my own titles (e.g. "Publications", "Talks"), so that I can include things the Default Sections don't cover.
38. As a job seeker, I want new Custom Sections listed in the editor after the Default Sections, in the order I add them, so that I know where to find them.
39. As a job seeker, I want to Disable a whole Section in one click, so that I can drop it from a tailored Resume quickly.
40. As a job seeker, I want re-Enabling a Section to restore each of its Entries' own Enabled states, so that I don't have to redo my choices inside it.

### Entries

41. As a job seeker, I want to add, edit and delete Entries in any Section, so that my Content stays current.
42. As a job seeker, I want to Disable individual Entries, so that I can leave an old job or project out of a particular Resume without deleting it.
43. As a job seeker, I want to keep several Summary Entries and Enable whichever I like, so that I can switch pitches per application.
44. As a job seeker, I want to decide the order of Entries within a Section, so that my most relevant work comes first. *(Not in v1: reordering comes later, with drag and drop.)*

### Entry shapes

45. As a job seeker, I want an Experience Entry to have company, role, location, start date, end date, and Bullets, so that I can describe each job fully.
46. As a job seeker, I want a Projects Entry to have name, link, tech stack, optional start and end dates, and Bullets, so that I can show off side projects.
47. As a job seeker, I want an Education Entry to have institution, degree, location, start date, end date, GPA/results, and Bullets, so that I can present my studies.
48. As a job seeker, I want a Skills Entry to have a label (e.g. "Languages") and a list of Skills, so that my skills are grouped neatly.
49. As a job seeker, I want a Summary Entry to be a single piece of Prose, so that I can write a short pitch.
50. As a job seeker, I want a Custom Section Entry to have title, subtitle, start date, end date, and Bullets, so that it fits most unusual content.

### Dates and Current

51. As a job seeker, I want to enter dates as a year with an optional month and optional day, so that I can be as precise as I like.
52. As a job seeker, I want to tick a checkbox (e.g. "I currently work here") to mark an Entry Current, so that it shows "Present" instead of an end date.
53. As a job seeker, I understand that marking an Entry Current removes its end date, so that the data is never contradictory.
54. As a job seeker, I want every date to be optional, so that Entries without dates still render cleanly.

### Bullets

55. As a job seeker, I want to add, edit and delete Bullets on an Entry, so that I can describe my achievements.
56. As a job seeker, I want to nest a Bullet under another Bullet (up to two levels), so that I can add supporting detail.
57. As a job seeker, I want to be prevented from nesting deeper than two levels, so that my resume stays readable and ATS-friendly.
58. As a job seeker, I want to decide the order of Bullets, so that my strongest points come first. *(Not in v1: reordering comes later, with drag and drop.)*
59. As a job seeker, I want to Disable individual Bullets, so that I can trim a job's description for one application without losing the text.
60. As a job seeker, I want Disabling a parent Bullet to hide its child Bullets too, while remembering their own states, so that I can toggle whole groups of points.

### Skills

61. As a job seeker, I want to add, edit, remove and reorder Skills within a Skills Entry, so that my list stays accurate.
62. As a job seeker, I want to Disable individual Skills (e.g. hide "PHP"), so that I can tailor my skills without duplicating whole groups.

### Prose formatting

63. As a job seeker, I want to use bold and italic in Summaries and Bullets, so that I can highlight key results (e.g. **40%**).
64. As a job seeker, I want to add links in Summaries and Bullets, so that I can point to live projects or write-ups.
65. As a job seeker, I want any other Markdown I type to appear as literal text, so that nothing unexpected happens to my content.
66. As a job seeker, I want unsafe links (e.g. `javascript:`) and raw HTML never to become live content, so that pasting untrusted text can't harm me.

### Preview, Theme and Export

67. As a job seeker, I want the preview to show only Enabled, non-Empty Content, so that I see exactly what will be exported.
68. As a job seeker, I want the preview rendered in a Theme on an A4 page, so that it looks like the final PDF.
69. As a job seeker, I want Custom Sections to render properly in the Theme, so that my extra content looks as polished as the rest.
70. As a job seeker, I want to Export my Resume as a PDF, so that I can attach it to applications.
71. As a job seeker, I want the exported PDF to match the preview exactly, so that there are no surprises.
72. As a job seeker, I want the editor UI to be absent from the exported PDF, so that only my resume is printed.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Stack**: Next.js, server-rendered by default; only the parts that need the browser (reading or writing Resumes, interactive editing) are Client Components (ADR 0002). Routes: a list page at `/resume-builder`, and an editor page at `/resume-builder/resumes/{uuid}`. The Resume id is a UUID generated client-side. "Create" first creates and persists a new Resume, then navigates to its editor.
- **Resume shape**: a Resume has three parts: Content, Theme Settings, and Metadata. Metadata holds id, Resume Title, created-at and last-edited-at. Theme Settings holds the Theme id and a Layout (ADR 0005): for each Zone, the ids of its Sections in order. The Zones are a fixed list: header, aside-left, main, aside-right, footer. A `null` Layout means the Theme's default, and in v1 the Layout is always `null` because rearranging Sections comes later. Accent colour, font and similar options will be added to Theme Settings later. Every stored Resume carries a schema version to allow future migrations (ADR 0002).
- **Content shape**: Content is a list of Sections. Its order only sets the editor's order: the Default Sections first, then Custom Sections in the order they were added. Where Sections appear on the page is decided by the Layout (ADR 0005, which supersedes ADR 0003). A Resume has exactly one of each Default Section; they can't be deleted, only left Empty or Disabled. Custom Sections can be added and deleted freely. Each Section has an id, a type (one of Header, Summary, Experience, Projects, Skills, Education, Custom), a title, an Enabled flag, a Pinned flag on the Header (Pinned = always first in its Zone), and an ordered list of Entries. The Header Section additionally holds name and headline; its Entries are contact items with a kind (email, phone, location, link) and value (links also carry a label).
- **Entry fields**, per Section type:
  - Summary: Prose text.
  - Experience: company, role, location, start date, end date, Current, Bullets.
  - Projects: name, link, tech stack, optional start date, end date, Current, Bullets.
  - Skills: label, ordered list of Skills (each with its own Enabled flag).
  - Education: institution, degree, location, start date, end date, Current, GPA/results, Bullets.
  - Custom: title, subtitle, start date, end date, Current, Bullets.
  - Every Entry, Bullet and Skill has an id and an Enabled flag.
- **Bullets**: an ordered list, where each Bullet may have an ordered list of child Bullets; the maximum depth is two levels, enforced by the Resume module.
- **Dates**: stored as a year with an optional month and optional day. Current is a real value on the Entry, not text; setting Current clears the end date. The checkbox label defaults to "I currently work here" for Experience, "I currently study here" for Education, and "Ongoing" elsewhere.
- **Enabled vs. Empty**: Disabling a parent never changes its children's own Enabled flags. Content is rendered only when it and all its ancestors are Enabled and it is not Empty. A Section with no renderable Entries is not rendered.
- **Resume module (deep module, main seam)**: a plain TypeScript module with no React and no browser dependencies that owns every rule above. Its interface covers: list Resumes (most recently edited first), get a Resume by id, create, Duplicate, rename (rejecting an empty Resume Title), delete; add Custom Sections; rename Sections (except the Header, whose title is fixed); delete Custom Sections (Default Sections can't be deleted); toggle Sections; add/edit/delete/toggle Entries (plus moving an Entry up or down, which has no UI in v1); add/edit/delete/nest/toggle Bullets; add/edit/delete/reorder/toggle Skills; set dates and Current; and a pure "renderable view" function that turns a Resume into only the Enabled, non-Empty Content a Theme should draw. Every mutation updates last-edited-at. Duplicate performs a deep copy with fresh ids for the Resume and all nested items.
- **Persistence**: the Resume module depends on a small persistence interface that is **async** from day one (ADR 0002). v1 provides a localStorage implementation. If two tabs edit the same Resume, the last write wins (acceptable for a local-only, single-user v1).
- **Autosave**: the editor calls the Resume module on every change; there is no Save button and no undo in v1.
- **Prose renderer (second seam)**: Prose is stored as Markdown source text (ADR 0004). A single renderer turns it into safe output, supporting only bold, italic and links. Any other syntax renders as literal text. Raw HTML is never passed through, and only http(s) and mailto link targets become links. Used for Summaries and Bullets only; every other field is plain text.
- **Themes**: v1 ships exactly one Theme. A Theme receives the renderable view and draws it; it contains no business logic. It defines which Zones it uses and a default Layout that places Sections into Zones by their type, Custom Sections included (rendered with the generic Entry shape). Within a Zone, a Pinned Section (the Header) always comes first. In v1 the Layout is always `null`, so the Theme always uses its default Layout.
- **Export**: uses the browser's print-to-PDF on the same HTML/CSS as the preview (ADR 0001). Page size is fixed at A4. Print CSS hides the editor and controls page breaks as well as possible.
- **Editor UI**: two panes, Content and preview. The Content pane edits the Header, Sections, Entries, Bullets and Skills and has Enabled toggles on each. An "add Custom Section" control adds a Custom Section. Default Sections are always present, so they are never offered.

## Testing Decisions

- **What makes a good test**: tests exercise external behaviour through a module's public interface, e.g. "Duplicate, then edit the copy; the original is unchanged". They never assert on internal structure or private helpers, so internals can be refactored freely.
- **Seam 1: the Resume module.** This is the main seam, tested with an in-memory implementation of the persistence interface. It covers: create (starting Sections, all Empty); Duplicate (independence, fresh ids, "(copy)" title); rename (non-empty, duplicates allowed); delete; list order; Header rules (exactly one, fixed title, can't be deleted); Default Sections can't be deleted; Section rename; Custom Sections added after the existing Sections, and deletable; Enabled and Disabled cascading without losing child states; Current clearing the end date; the two-level Bullet nesting limit; last-edited-at updating; and the renderable view excluding Disabled and Empty Content.
- **Seam 2: the Prose renderer.** Tested with input/output cases: bold, italic and links render; unsupported Markdown renders literally; `javascript:` and other non-http(s)/mailto links do not become links; raw HTML and script tags appear as text.
- **Not tested in v1**: React components, the Theme's visual output, the localStorage implementation beyond a thin smoke test, and end-to-end browser flows.
- **Tooling**: Vitest as the test runner. There is no prior art in the repo; these will be the first tests.

## Out of Scope

- Accounts, sign-in, sync, and premium Themes/features.
- Linting or feedback on resume content (the name "Linted" is only a brand for now).
- Exporting or importing a Resume as JSON (backup or transfer).
- Rearranging Sections on the page (ADR 0005). The Layout is stored but always `null` in v1. When rearranging arrives, it also brings: Ghosted Sections in the preview (Disabled or Empty Sections shown as faded titles, left out of the Export); applying a stored Layout (ignoring unknown ids, and placing Sections missing from it by type); Duplicate remapping the Layout to the copy's new Section ids; deleting a Custom Section also removing it from the Layout; and switching Theme resetting the Layout.
- Repeating a Default Section (e.g. a second Experience Section).
- Reordering Entries and Bullets. It comes later, with drag and drop; v1 has no reordering controls.
- More than one Theme; Theme options such as accent colour, fonts or density; page sizes other than A4.
- DOCX export, plain-text/ATS export, and public share links.
- Undo/redo.
- Formatting beyond bold, italic and links; formatting in non-Prose fields.
- IndexedDB storage and images (e.g. profile photos).
- Merging the editor and preview into a single view.
- Landing page content (Next.js was chosen partly so one can be server-rendered later).

## Further Notes

- The glossary in `CONTEXT.md` is the source of truth for terms (Resume, Section, Entry, Bullet, Skill, Enabled, Empty, Current, Pinned, Prose, Theme, Zone, Layout, Export). Use those words in code and UI copy.
- ADRs: 0001 (PDF Export via browser print), 0002 (Next.js and localStorage), 0003 (Sections stored as an ordered list, superseded by 0005), 0004 (Prose stored as Markdown), 0005 (Layout in Theme Settings).
- A second Theme is planned right after v1. Building it will test the Theme contract, so any v1 assumptions that are specific to the first Theme should be kept out of the Resume module.

Sourced from bson's releases.

1.1.6

The MongoDB Node.js team is pleased to announce version 1.1.6 of the bson module!

The BSON library was written prior to the invention of the BigInt type in Javascript ecosystem. As a result the library was not able to serialize the type properly and silently failed to correctly maintain the bigint value. With this update, the library will now throw an error if it detects a bigint value. However, we've also added to/fromBigInt helper methods to the long class, please note that numbers will be clamped to int64 bit width.

const bytes = BSON.serialize({ myBigNumber: Long.fromBigInt(23n) })
const doc = BSON.deserialize(bytes)
doc.myBigNumber.toBigInt() === 23n // true

New Feature

  • [NODE-2378] - Return error when failing to serialize bigint type and add Long class helpers

Documentation

  • API: https://github.com/mongodb/js-bson#readme
  • Changelog: https://github.com/mongodb/js-bson/blob/master/HISTORY.md#change-log

We invite you to try the bson library immediately, and report any issues to the NODE project. Thanks very much to all the community members who contributed to this release!

v1.1.4

The MongoDB Node.js team is pleased to announce version 1.1.4 of the bson module!

This patch release resolves an issue with BSON serialization with invalid _bsontype, originally reported by @​xiaofen9. MongoDB will be issuing a CVE for this vulnerability, and we recommend that all users pin their version of the bson module to 1.1.4 or higher.

2.4.0

Related blog post: https://socket.io/blog/socket-io-2-4-0/

Features (from Engine.IO)

  • add support for all cookie options (19cc582)
  • disable perMessageDeflate by default (5ad2736)

Bug Fixes

  • security: do not allow all origins by default (f78a575)
  • properly overwrite the query sent in the handshake (d33a619)

:warning: BREAKING CHANGE :warning:

Previously, CORS was enabled by default, which meant that a Socket.IO server sent the necessary CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-xxx) to any domain. This will not be the case anymore, and you now have to explicitly enable it.

Please note that you are not impacted if:

  • you are using Socket.IO v2 and the origins option to restrict the list of allowed domains
  • you are using Socket.IO v3 (disabled by default)

This commit also removes the support for '*' matchers and protocol-less URL:

io.origins('https://example.com:443'); => io.origins(['https://example.com']);
io.origins('localhost:3000');          => io.origins(['http://localhost:3000']);
io.origins('http://localhost:*');      => io.origins(['http://localhost:3000']);
io.origins('*:3000');                  => io.origins(['http://localhost:3000']);

To restore the previous behavior (please use with caution):

io.origins((_, callback) => {
  callback(null, true);
});

See also:

  • https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS
  • https://socket.io/docs/v3/handling-cors/

items.body:
A player who has joined later in the game (or an existing player who has refreshed their app page) cannot see mortgaged properties in the board UI.
This is because no exposed state of 'isMortgaged' is released from server end for the properties.

Consider creating a state for the mapData that would include 'isMortgaged' status, 'owner' and other required details.

Note: A not-so-good alternative would be to create a separate array for mortgaged properties.
